gaps.fact: Melon B as the official name the Court now prints for Muscadet's grape, with Melon de Bourgogne as the former name: the Codex teaches Melon de Bourgogne throughout, and Melon B appears only as a wrong option in i-qy5eckga, never as Muscadet's grape.
Domaine Huet, the Court's named Vouvray producer, stands first in the article's producer list and is asked in no question of either bank.

The Court's History cell is the name of a living Savennières grower, the biodynamic pioneer of Coulée de Serrant; the house rule keeps the name out of our copy, so the Codex teaches the estate and its biodynamic lead and a candidate must attach the Court's name to it from the guide.

Pairings keyed to the sweetness levels of Chenin Blanc (sec, demi-sec, moelleux) are given in the article's wine notes and asked in no question; the banks pair Muscadet, Sancerre and goat cheese only.

errors.where: js/regions/france.json, records.loire.law.classification: "Muscadet has ten crus communaux, nine in Sèvre et Maine plus Champtoceaux, the first three recognised in 2011" (the same count in law.tiers, "Ten named villages", and in the Crus communaux place note, which lists La Haye-Fouassière, Vallet and Champtoceaux with the rest)
errors.claim: Ten Muscadet crus communaux are recognised.
errors.correction: Seven are recognised in the appellation rules: Clisson, Gorges and Le Pallet from 2011, then Château-Thébaud, Goulaine, Monnières-Saint-Fiacre and Mouzillon-Tillières. Champtoceaux (under Muscadet Coteaux de la Loire), La Haie-Fouassière and Vallet were still proposals when the INAO put them to public consultation from 25 August to 25 October 2025, and a tasting report of February 2026 still counted seven; count the three only once their amended rules are published. The Village stem c-uw7cv5tw is worded safely ("further villages have been approved since").
errors.source: INAO, avis de consultation publique, trois dénominations géographiques complémentaires Muscadet (inao.gouv.fr, August 2025); thewinedoctor.com, Muscadet crus communaux tasting, February 2026; vinsdeloire.fr, Muscadet Sèvre et Maine crus communaux.

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 59 (Loire), Village 37 (Loire), 96 in all. Beyond the map, Food & Pairing asks Muscadet with oysters and goat cheese with Sauvignon, Grapes & Labels asks Breton, and Geography & Maps asks where the Loire rises. Every appellation, grape, soil and winemaking fact in the Court's two columns is taught and most are asked; the thin cells are the two producers and the pairing by sweetness. One error found, in the article's count of the Muscadet crus communaux (ten where seven are in law, the other three still proposals in 2025); otherwise, across the chapters, the article and the 96 stems, Quarts de Chaume Grand Cru 2011, Chaume Premier Cru, the three first crus communaux of 2011, Montlouis 1938, Saint-Bris aside, Savennières permitting demi-sec and moelleux, Vouvray's Orbois allowance and Noble-Joué's three Pinots all hold. One search spent, on the Muscadet crus communaux, which the Court's cells do not name; nothing in the Court's Loire cells is a dated law or classification that has moved since 8.2023.
